claims.text: The presence of ferromagnetic ground states can be determined using ab initio molecular dynamics together with the PBE generalized-gradient approximation.
The target materials are ferromagnetic materials.
Ab initio molecular dynamics is the proposed simulation intervention.
The Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof functional is used within the generalized-gradient approximation for exchange-correlation energy.
Electronic structure mediates the effect of the simulation on the magnetic-state determination.
Ab initio molecular dynamics provides an accurate description of electronic structure.
An accurate electronic-structure description allows determination of whether the ground state is ferromagnetic.
The proposed method predicts the presence or absence of a ferromagnetic ground state.
Non-magnetic or paramagnetic states serve as the baseline.
The simulation is limited to the material's electronic structure.
The simulation does not account for other factors that may influence magnetic properties.
Simulation accuracy depends on the selected exchange-correlation functional.
Simulation accuracy depends on the quality of the input parameters.
The hypothesis can be tested by varying the exchange-correlation functional and measuring magnetic moment and electronic density of states.
Failure to converge to a ferromagnetic ground state with different exchange-correlation functionals falsifies the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention is ab initio molecular dynamics, which includes atomic dynamics, whereas the boundary describes the simulation as limited solely to electronic structure.

The predicted outcome includes determining that a ferromagnetic ground state is absent, but the falsification rule treats failure to obtain a ferromagnetic state as falsification rather than as a possible valid negative result.
